name: Marhaenism
summary: Marhaenism is the socialist nationalism devised by Sukarno in the late 1920s and 1930s and used as the guiding ideology of the Indonesian National Party. It applies a Marxist reading of oppression to Indonesia, where most poor people are small owner-cultivators (marhaen) rather than a proletariat, and ties national independence to the end of capitalism and imperialism. Its pillars are socio-nationalism, socio-democracy (political plus economic democracy) and gotong royong, later joined to Pancasila, with belief in God kept and communism and liberal capitalism both rejected as models.
scope: Sukarno's Marhaenism as documented in his 1957 PNI anniversary speech Marhaen and Proletarian, scholarship and encyclopedic accounts of his 1930s writings, and the 1945 Pancasila formulation, as carried by the PNI and later Sukarnoist movements. Excludes the later Suharto-era Pancasila state doctrine and loose uses of the name. Many statements are modern and were never addressed by Sukarno, so many answers are inferences marked low confidence.

sources.usedFor: The 1945 five principles: nationalism, internationalism, consensus democracy, social welfare, belief in God, gotong royong.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sukarno attacks liberal capitalism and wants production for needs before the market, though small-scale trade by Marhaen is not condemned.

public-ownership.rationale: Marhaenism aims at Indonesian control of land and production against foreign finance capital; state/public control of key sectors followed under guided economy, though small private ownership stays.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are part of the Marhaen mass whose organized mass action is central to the struggle.

property-fundamental.rationale: Small ownership of land and tools is protected, but property as an absolute right is denied in favor of economic democracy and national control of capital.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Sukarno condemns investment/finance capital as the engine of imperialism and pauperization, implying tight control of big corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Cutting support for the poor contradicts the central aim of lifting the Marhaen from poverty and the demand that needs be met.

worker-ownership.rationale: Marhaenism stresses ownership of small means of production by the people themselves, but does not demand worker collective ownership of firms as Marx did.

strong-leader.rationale: Sukarno criticized multiparty parliament as unstable and introduced Guided Democracy under strong presidential leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Marhaenism seeks to build an independent socialist Indonesian state and rejects any anti-state position.

decide-locally.rationale: Sukarno championed a unitary state spanning the former Dutch East Indies and consolidated central authority against regional rebellions.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pancasila gives belief in God a public place but Sukarno opposed a sharia state; adherents split between a religious and a secular reading.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Marhaenism rests on Indonesian culture and Pancasila, rejecting wholesale adoption of foreign models.

gradual-change.rationale: Sukarno called for revolutionary mass action and a revolution lasting decades, not gradual respect for established colonial institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Sukarno used the UN stage and championed internationalism, but also withdrew Indonesia from the UN in 1965 and distrusted Western-dominated bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Sukarno blames liberal trade and finance capital for pauperization; free trade is treated as an instrument of imperialism.

nation-first.rationale: Independence is the golden bridge and national interest guides policy, though Pancasila also holds internationalism, so only moderate.

open-borders.rationale: Pancasila couples internationalism with a firm national unity; open borders is not an aim.

revolution-justified.rationale: Sukarno described the struggle as revolutionary mass action against colonialism and imperialism.

central-planning.rationale: Sukarno rejected both capitalism and Soviet-style models and spoke of Indonesian methods; planning was used in practice but not as doctrine.

socialized-markets.rationale: Marhaenism accepts small-scale ownership and exchange but does not state a view on market socialism.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Marhaen ideal is the small owner of land and tools who stays independent; productive assets should be widely held by ordinary Indonesians.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Sukarno kept the proletarian concept but did not call for abolition of money or wages; his goal was a Marhaen-owned economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A nationalist socialism that wants national economic control would not abolish central banks to the market.

one-party-rule.rationale: Sukarno favored a national front and later wished to bury the parties, but he was not a single-party ideologue; PNI competed in elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Marhaenism wants a republic; Sukarno sought a socialist republic.

democracy-best.rationale: Sukarno called parliamentary democracy the bourgeois philosophy and replaced it with Guided Democracy, yet kept popular sovereignty and socio-democracy as the goal.

direct-votes.rationale: Pancasila democracy is musyawarah mufakat by deliberation, not direct plebiscites.

workers-councils.rationale: Sukarno proposed a National Council and gotong royong institutions rather than workers' councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Sukarno built a unitary Indonesia and suppressed regional rebellions.

natural-rulers.rationale: Marhaenism is egalitarian and populist; not directly addressed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Revolutionary mass action and struggle against imperialism are central, though Sukarno stressed non-cooperation and mass action more than arms.

separate-church-state.rationale: Sukarno rejected a sharia state but made belief in God one of Pancasila's principles, so strict separation is not the Pancasila model.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Sukarno rejected making sharia binding in the constitution, favoring a unified non-confessional state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pancasila nationalism includes everyone living in Indonesia and rejects ethnic dominance.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Sukarno tied independence to the Marxist view of history as struggle between oppressed and oppressors, adapted without dogmatism and with nation prominent.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The sama rasa sama rata society aims at equality of feeling and status, i.e. broad material equality.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Sukarno reflected on nature as reflecting God but no environmental ethic is stated.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Capital should meet needs and produce surplus rather than be hoarded, and economic democracy limits ownership; small property is protected.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Sukarno said he was not a communist and rejected copying Soviet or Western models, but gave no analysis of the USSR as state capitalist.

collective-defense.rationale: Sukarno championed non-alignment and opposed Western military pacts such as SEATO.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Sukarno as president claimed to stand above parties yet was the movement's leading figure; no doctrine.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Sukarno used force against regional rebellions in defense of a unitary state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Sukarno favored a unitary state over federal or special-system arrangements.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A republican, anti-feudal ideology; Sukarno rejected monarchy and divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Despite Guided Democracy's concentration of power, the ideology does not endorse a ruler above law.

leader-cult.rationale: Sukarno was honoured as Great Leader of the Revolution, but this was a personal cult rather than ideological doctrine.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pancasila nationalism rejects ethnic claims, although Sukarno pursued Greater Indonesia and Malaya confrontation on anti-colonial grounds.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Pancasila stresses religious freedom and rejects sharia in the constitution.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Sukarno had pan-Asian and Malay-world ideas (Maphilindo) but it is not a Marhaenist principle.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Sukarno kept Marxist historical materialism as a method while separating it from philosophical materialism and adding culture and belief in God.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Sukarno urged national economic self-reliance but not a closed colonial bloc.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Marhaenism emphasizes mass action by the Marhaen masses and non-cooperation rather than a small armed vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-feudal republican nationalism; Sukarno sought a socialist republic of equals.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Indonesia as a unity of land and collective feeling is central to the ideology.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Sukarno condemned Dutch imperialism as exploitation of man by man.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism is a core principle (socio-nationalism) and Sukarno promoted national indoctrination in Guided Democracy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Sukarno saw capitalism as imperialist and exploitative and fascism as its desperate last attempt to survive, not as adapting.

delink-world-market.rationale: Sukarno criticized imperialism but stressed independence rather than delinking, and sought partners among non-aligned states.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Sukarno's account of the Marhaen as nearly all Indonesians is about the colony; he did not analyze workers in rich countries.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Contrary to equality and unity of Pancasila nationalism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Sukarno distrusted liberal parliamentary frameworks, yet the sources record no view on entrenched rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Republican; ruler chosen by the people, though through deliberation and not purely competitive elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Pancasila democracy is deliberation toward consensus (mufakat), but it does not give individuals veto powers.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Revolutionary mass action against colonial rule; not framed for domestic rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sukarno called parliamentary democracy bourgeois and replaced it with Guided Democracy.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Marhaenism seeks structural equality rather than paternalist duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Marhaenism is a struggle ideology demanding active mass political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Marhaenism has no theory of culture as pacification; Sukarno used culture to mobilize rather than as a critique.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Sukarno argued Dutch finance-capital imperialism suppressed Indonesian skills and purchasing power, impoverishing the people.

party-own-road.rationale: Sukarno insisted on an Indonesian road, rejecting uncritical adoption of Soviet or Western models.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-reliance was one of the Marhaenist struggle principles, with independence required before prosperity.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Sukarno pursued West Irian but no general doctrine on lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Pancasila nationalism includes all living in Indonesia; not framed this way.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Sukarno described fascism as capitalism's last gasp, but made no constitutional claim.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Sukarno condemned fascism as a capitalist tool while declining to condemn communism; he cooperated with the PKI under Nasakom.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Sukarno argued parliamentary democracy was not suited to Indonesia and developed musyawarah-based Guided Democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Sukarno gave the army a role under Guided Democracy, but it is not an ideological principle.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Opposition to foreign finance capital and later nationalization of Dutch firms.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Recallable mandates are a council-communist idea; the sources show Sukarno using consensus deliberation without binding mandates.

single-official-language.rationale: Sukarno promoted Bahasa Indonesia as unifying language, though no ban on others is documented.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Marhaenism seeks Indonesian control of land and production against foreign capital.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Sukarno opposed great-power domination and championed non-alignment.

corporate-influence.rationale: Capital's power over politics is part of the anti-capitalist critique, though stated mainly regarding colonial finance capital.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Pancasila emphasizes community, unity and duty.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-imperialism and non-alignment emphasize sovereignty against outside interference.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Pancasila nationalism rejects ethnic or religious scapegoating.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Contrary to the religious and traditional values of Pancasila.

local-production.rationale: Households first meeting their own needs before the market is stated, but not local production generally.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Sukarno stressed sovereignty but also used UN and Bandung forums, and the sources record no stance on legal precedence.

religious-nation.rationale: Pancasila is explicitly inclusive of all religions; Sukarno rejected sharia as a basis for the state.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejects deference to great powers; non-aligned and anti-imperial.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Unitary state; regional rebellions were suppressed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marhaen own their land and tools; private possessions are not threatened and means of production are not wholly collectivized.

defeat-communism.rationale: Sukarno rejected anti-communism and brought the PKI into Nasakom.

religion-illusion.rationale: Belief in God is the first Pancasila principle and Sukarno separated historical materialism from philosophical materialism.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Sukarno saw capitalism as impoverishing Indonesia, although he used some Marxist history in which it precedes socialism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are outside Marhaenist sources, with no basis for a stance.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Gotong royong is central, but the model is a national state not small self-governing communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Transmigration happened in practice but is not part of the ideology.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sukarno presented Pancasila and Marhaenism as a third way, claiming "I am not a communist" while condemning capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Sukarno's claim to West Irian rested on Dutch East Indies succession rather than historical or religious ties, so the sources do not support a general stance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Guided Democracy banned some parties (Masyumi) but ideology promotes unity and consensus.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Sukarno denounced colonial exploitation and finance-capital imperialism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contrary to Pancasila's religiously neutral state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Socio-democracy and gotong royong emphasize mass participation and economic as well as political democracy.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Sukarno sought synthesis of nationalism, Islam and Marxism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Belief in God is a principle but sovereignty rests on the people through deliberation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Sukarno built armed forces and defended independence by force.

rich-first.rationale: Sama rasa sama rata equality and rejection of capital hoarding contradict letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Sukarno led non-alignment and a third path between Western and Eastern blocs.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sukarno denounced foreign finance capital and in 1960s broke with the IMF and World Bank.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is outside Marhaenism; the sources discuss only colonial domination.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Sukarno held that liberal democracy is the bourgeois philosophy, offering formal freedoms without economic equality ("the stomach does not wait").

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Indonesian law restricted interfaith marriage but Marhaenist sources are silent on it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Sukarno was a modernist on Islam, but the sources document no Marhaenist doctrine on reinterpreting religious law.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sukarno held that concentrated finance capital and the bourgeoisie shape politics and suppress the people.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Belief in God is a Pancasila principle.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nasakom sought to share power among nationalists, religious groups and communists; not formal consociationalism.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Social justice is assigned to collective and state action.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Sukarno-era organizations had youth wings but the sources document no doctrine on drilled national-service youth movements.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sukarno condemned foreign bases as a form of imperialism and neo-colonialism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Marhaenism aims at development and prosperity for the Marhaen; industrial society is blamed only in its capitalist form.

restore-past-order.rationale: Marhaenism is forward-looking revolutionary nationalism, building a new socialist republic.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marhaenism is explicitly a struggle ideology and Sukarno insisted on Pancasila and Marhaen principles.

direct-action.rationale: Nulled: the statement now asks whether direct action should replace electoral politics (reworded 2026-11-10, Codex review). This answer rested on direct action used alongside elections or on a mixed record, which does not support agreeing that it should replace them; its sources need re-reading against the new text.

reviewHistory.rationale: Revolutionary mass action and non-cooperation were core Marhaenist methods, though PNI also contested elections.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled: the statement now asks whether direct action should replace electoral politics (reworded 2026-11-10, Codex review). This answer rested on direct action used alongside elections or on a mixed record, which does not support agreeing that it should replace them; its sources need re-reading against the new text.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marhaen are specialized farmers, workers and traders; no abolition is proposed.

production-for-use.rationale: People should meet their own needs before serving the market, and capital should produce for needs rather than be hoarded.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Sukarno described investment capital as extracting profit by suppressing wages and purchasing power; this is mostly about colonial finance capital.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Sukarno presented Marhaenism as Marxism applied to Indonesia and worked with the PKI, but he made the broad Marhaen mass, not the proletariat alone, the subject of the revolution, so he did not endorse a class dictatorship without forcefully rejecting it.

collective-farming.rationale: The Marhaen ideal is the small farmer who owns land and tools, not collective farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Sukarno linked finance capital to imperialism and colonial subjugation; interimperial war is not specifically discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Contrary to a nationalist, participatory ideology.

positive-liberty.rationale: Sukarno: "the stomach does not wait", so freedom requires meeting material needs alongside political rights (socio-democracy).

media-academia-power.rationale: Marhaenist texts name colonial capital and the bourgeois parliament as the powers over the people, not universities or media, so no stance follows.

organic-representation.rationale: Guided Democracy introduced functional groups; gotong royong and consensus favor representation of social groups.

total-state.rationale: Guided Democracy was authoritarian but the ideology is not totalist; belief in God and individual plots persist.

national-rebirth.rationale: Sukarno called Indonesia's revolution a rebirth, symphony of destruction and creation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Sukarno's West Irian and Malaysia campaigns were anti-colonial, but the ideology doesn't endorse expansion in general.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Sukarno's writings contain no theory of knowledge and power; he only separated Marxist historical method from philosophical materialism.

universal-morality.rationale: Pancasila includes humanism and belief in God, but no epistemology stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Gotong royong and musyawarah mufakat aim at a common consensus rather than balancing interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Sukarno backed Palestinian causes and refused Israeli participation in Asian Games, though not a doctrine of Marhaenism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Socio-democracy combines political and economic democracy, implying democratic say over economic life.

economic-freedom.rationale: Sukarno said parliamentary democracy cannot deliver socialism and that economic needs cannot wait.

national-self-determination.rationale: Independence (Indonesia Merdeka) is the golden bridge and absolute precondition.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Belief in God is a Pancasila principle and Sukarno kept religion in his synthesis.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nasakom and gotong royong favor national cooperation, yet the Marhaen are a class in struggle with imperialist capital; split.

dominated-front.rationale: Sukarno championed the Non-Aligned Movement, Asian-African solidarity and the New Emerging Forces against Old Established Forces.

workers-nation.rationale: Marhaenism ties class struggle to national liberation of the whole Marhaen people.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Sukarno's Marhaenism sets no doctrine on gender roles; adherents split between traditionalists and the women's wing of the national movement.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Sukarno viewed the colonial state and parliament as instruments of the bourgeoisie, in a Marxist vocabulary.

national-mission.rationale: Sukarno saw Pancasila as a universal alternative to West and East, but not a mission to spread.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist stance against bourgeois politicians and parties.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past security-force abuses is outside Marhaenist sources, with no basis for a stance.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Sukarno held that Indonesian socialism could be built on its own national road.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Pancasila leaves family law to religious communities in practice while seeking national unity, so adherents lack a settled position.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Pancasila belief in God supports religious education in schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Sukarno said Indonesia must find its own road and not copy Soviet models, and did not theorize the state's strength under encirclement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Popular sovereignty via musyawarah, though Sukarno also asserted guided leadership.

trade-surplus.rationale: Sukarno wanted Indonesians to control production, but no doctrine on export surpluses appears in the sources.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Sukarno banned Masyumi and PSI in 1960 but also defended the PKI.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Marhaenism rests on freedom from colonial and capitalist domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Guided Democracy concentrated power in the president.

vanguard-party.rationale: Sukarno rejected a Leninist vanguard and spoke of mass action by the Marhaen masses.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Marhaenism is an ideology of the poor small people, the Marhaen.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sukarno blamed colonial finance capital for pauperization.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Pancasila democracy proposes deliberation and consensus; lotteries for office are not mentioned in the sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Sukarno declared martial law in 1957 and used emergency powers.

party-controls-media.rationale: Guided Democracy curtailed press but not a doctrinal stance.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The PNI was a mass party but the sources record no doctrine on binding party members to decisions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential system under the 1945 constitution that Sukarno restored in 1959.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is an internal religious matter outside Marhaenism and Pancasila's religious neutrality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sukarno was named president for life in 1963, but not doctrine.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Non-alignment and rejection of foreign bases.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Marhaen farmer is central but no moral claim about rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Sukarno himself was a university-educated engineer leading the movement, and the sources record no anti-intellectual strain.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Sukarno opposed civilizing tutelage and rejected copying any model; claims equality of nations.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources record no position on capital punishment; Sukarno's governments used it against rebels but the ideology is silent.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is a modern debate outside Marhaenism, and Pancasila religiosity would pull against it while equality of the sexes pulls for it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Pancasila nationalism fostered Bahasa Indonesia as a unifier while claiming unity in diversity, and the sources record no stance on minority-language schooling.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Sukarno condemned finance capital and neo-colonial debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sukarno insisted that independence is only a golden bridge and that colonialism and imperialism are not yet dead without socialist transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Sukarno called for a return to the 1945 constitution, but a constituent assembly was elected in 1955; not doctrine.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Guided Democracy limited freedoms in the name of national development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sukarno wanted self-reliance; no duty of aid stated.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are beyond the sources; Sukarno's 1960s Indonesia explored them, but the ideology has no doctrine.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inference: the 1957 speech presumes organised mass struggle through the PNI, though it does not address small informal groups as an alternative.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Marhaenism is a material analysis of class and imperialism, though belief in God is kept; not framed as cosmic struggle.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socio-democracy means political and economic democracy for the Marhaen and the people, so the poor majority must hold real power, though Sukarno rejects the narrow proletarian framing.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Belief in God is kept in Pancasila as the first principle, and Marhaenism rejects purely materialist communism.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sukarno's Indonesian nation was a territorial, anti-colonial community of many languages and religions, unified by shared history of Dutch rule, not by a single language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Sukarno's Pancasila stressed one Indonesian nation and consensus democracy; separate religious electorates would cut against national unity, though he balanced Islam, nationalism and Marxism (NASAKOM).

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Sukarno repeatedly warned of imperialist and neocolonial powers undermining Indonesia, with regional rebellions in the 1950s seen as foreign-backed.

arms-reduction.rationale: Sukarno backed non-alignment and peace diplomacy but also armed confrontation (West Irian, Malaysia) and a large military, so adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialism is central to Marhaenism, which ties independence to ending imperialist and capitalist exploitation of poor nations.

farm-price-support.rationale: Marhaenism centres on small owner-cultivators exploited by capital and moneylenders, so state or cooperative protection of them follows from its core.

workers-own-party.rationale: The PNI was built as the party of the marhaen masses, independent of colonial-era parties, though Marhaenism rejects a purely proletarian class party.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Sukarno's nationalism embraced one Indonesian language uniting the archipelago's regions under a single name and national identity.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Pancasila, which Marhaenism joined, keeps belief in God and treats the recognised faiths equally in the state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Sukarno's socio-democracy demands economic as well as political democracy, so elections alone do not make a democracy.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Belief in God is kept as a Marhaenist pillar, and the sources locate oppression in capitalism and imperialism rather than religion.

indirect-election.rationale: Sukarno's Guided Democracy and consensus (musyawarah) with functional groups replaced direct party competition.

national-church-status.rationale: Pancasila affirms belief in God without privileging one religion in law.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Sukarno's Guided Democracy set aside party competition in favour of consensus around the leader.

national-resource-control.rationale: Marhaenism ties independence to the end of imperialism and capitalist control of Indonesia's wealth.

multipolar-world.rationale: Anti-imperialism is core to Marhaenism, and Sukarno carried it into non-alignment and opposition to domination by any bloc.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Socio-nationalism is a pillar: nationalism rooted in the interests of the poor, with independence tied to the end of capitalism and imperialism.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Marhaenism rejected communism as a model and kept belief in God, so a communist party directing a market economy does not fit it.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Cutting support for the poor contradicts the central aim of lifting the Marhaen from poverty and the demand that needs be met. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A nation's poor should be defined by whether they own their own tools and land rather than only by whether they sell their labor.
missingStatements.rationale: Sukarno's core claim is that the marhaen is a poor small owner-cultivator, distinct from the Marxist proletarian.

missingStatements.text: Mutual cooperation (gotong royong) should be the organising principle of society and the economy rather than competition.
missingStatements.rationale: Sukarno condensed Pancasila into gotong royong and proposed a gotong-royong cabinet.

notes: Stated positions cluster on anti-capitalism, anti-imperialism, nationalism, mass struggle, rejection of both liberalism and communism, and Pancasila religiosity. Sources opened were Wikipedia, a scholarly abstract and an OCR translation of one primary speech; Indonesia Menggugat and Mencapai Indonesia Merdeka were not accessible.
